questions.title: Recursive Factorial
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long factorial(int n)

It must return n! computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): factorial(n) = n * factorial(n-1) with the base case returning 1 for n <= 1.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with n!.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 20 (n! fits in a 64-bit integer)

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fib(int n)

It must return the n-th Fibonacci number computed RECURSIVELY (no loops), with fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1, so fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2).

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with fib(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Digit Sum by Recursion
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int digit_sum(int n)

It must return the sum of the decimal digits of n, computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): digit_sum(n) = n % 10 + digit_sum(n / 10) with the base case returning n when n < 10. digit_sum(0) = 0.

Input Format:
One line with the non-negative integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the digit sum.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 2000000000

questions.title: Reverse a String Recursively
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void reverse_string(char s[], int len)

It must reverse the string s (of exactly len characters) IN PLACE, recursively: swap the outer pair s[lo]/s[hi] and recurse on the inner substring (no loops).

Input Format:
One line with a token (no spaces) and its length is passed to you.

Output Format:
One line with the reversed string.

Constraints:
1 <= len <= 100000

questions.title: Recursive GCD
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long gcd(long long a, long long b)

It must return the greatest common divisor of a and b using the RECURSIVE Euclidean algorithm (no loops): gcd(a, b) = a when b == 0, otherwise gcd(b, a % b).

Input Format:
One line with two integers a and b (not both zero).

Output Format:
One line with gcd(a, b).

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 1000000000000, not both zero

questions.title: Count All Subsets
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long subset_count(int n)

An n-element set has exactly 2^n subsets (the empty set included). Return the count computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): subset_count(0) = 1 and subset_count(n) = 2 * subset_count(n-1) — each element doubles the number of subsets.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with 2^n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Recursive Power Function
questions.description:
A finance model grows an amount by repeated multiplication and wants the exponentiation done by pure recursion — each level of the recursion tree multiplies once more until the exponent bottoms out.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long power(int base, int exp)

It must return base raised to exp, computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): power(base, 0) = 1 and power(base, exp) = base * power(base, exp - 1).

Input Format:
One line with the integers base and exp.

Output Format:
One line with base^exp.

Constraints:
|base| <= 30, 0 <= exp <= 15

questions.title: Ticket Code Palindrome
questions.description:
A ticketing system validates codes that must read the same in both directions. The check is done by recursion: compare the outer characters and shrink inward — the call stack remembers where to resume.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_palindrome(char s[], int len)

It must return 1 when s is a palindrome (reads identically forwards and backwards), else 0. Implement it recursively by comparing s[lo] with s[hi] and recursing inward (no loops).

Input Format:
One line with a token (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= len <= 100000

questions.title: Sensor Batch Total
questions.description:
A field device batches sensor readings and sums them with a divide-and-conquer recursion instead of a loop — each call splits the batch until single readings remain.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long array_sum(int arr[], int n)

It must return the sum of arr[0..n-1] computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): array_sum of nothing is 0, otherwise arr[n-1] + array_sum of the first n-1 readings.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Peak Load Finder
questions.description:
An uptime dashboard finds the day's peak load recursively: the max of n readings is the larger of the last reading and the max of the rest — a recursion that walks the call stack down to a single reading.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int array_max(int arr[], int n)

It must return the maximum of arr[0..n-1] computed RECURSIVELY (no loops): array_max of one element is that element, otherwise the larger of arr[n-1] and array_max of the first n-1 readings.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Count Subsets Summing to S
questions.description:
A warehouse picker wonders in how many ways a target weight S can be assembled from a set of item weights, using each item at most once (order does not matter, the empty selection counts when S = 0). The answer must come from pure include/exclude recursion.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_subsets_sum(int arr[], int n, int S)

It must return the number of subsets of arr[0..n-1] whose values sum to exactly S. Implement it recursively: for each item either include it (recurse with S - arr[i]) or skip it (recurse with S); NO loops are allowed in your code.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: S.

Output Format:
One line with the number of qualifying subsets.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= value <= 100, 0 <= S <= 2000

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Moves
questions.description:
A puzzle app animates the Tower of Hanoi and needs the exact move script produced by the classic recursion: move n-1 disks aside, move the biggest disk, move them back. Each move is one line.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void hanoi(int n, char from, char to, char aux)

It must PRINT one line per move, in the order the moves happen, formatted exactly as:

    disk X: FROM->TO

Solve it recursively: hanoi(n-1, from, aux, to), then move disk n from the FROM peg to the TO peg (print the line), then hanoi(n-1, aux, to, from). The harness calls hanoi(n, 'A', 'C', 'B') and prints nothing else. No loops are allowed in your code.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
2^n - 1 lines, one per move, in execution order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8

questions.title: Distinct Permutations of a Multiset
questions.description:
A badge printer arranges engraved plates in a row. Identical plates make arrangements indistinguishable, so the printer needs the number of DISTINCT permutations of the multiset: n! divided by the factorial of every value's multiplicity.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long distinct_perms(int arr[], int n)

It must return n! / (c1! * c2! * ...), where each ci is how many times one distinct value occurs. Count multiplicities with nested loops (do NOT sort and do NOT use qsort; handle each distinct value exactly once).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct permutations.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12, 0 <= value <= 100

questions.title: Fibonacci Call Counter
questions.description:
A CS tutor visualizes the recursion tree of the naive Fibonacci: fib(n) spawns fib(n-1) and fib(n-2). To size the drawing, count how many function calls the naive recursion makes in total — the tree of calls IS the recursion tree.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fib_calls(int n)

It must return the total number of calls made by the naive recursion for fib(n), counting the initial call: fib_calls(0) = 1, fib_calls(1) = 1, and fib_calls(n) = 1 + fib_calls(n-1) + fib_calls(n-2). Implement it recursively (no loops).

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the total call count.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Recursive Binary Search
questions.description:
A dictionary service looks up words with binary search implemented as recursion: examine the middle slot, then recurse into the surviving half — the call stack replaces the loop.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int rbsearch(int arr[], int lo, int hi, int target)

The array arr[lo..hi] is sorted ascending with distinct values. It must return the 0-based index of target, or -1 when absent. Implement it recursively: if lo > hi return -1, otherwise compare against the middle and recurse into one half. NO loops are allowed in your code.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n sorted distinct integers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the index or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |target| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Print Permutations in Lex Order
questions.description:
A locker-assignment tool lists every way to order n distinct items (the input already lists them ascending) so the listing comes out in lexicographic order — a classic backtracking walk: pick the smallest unused item next, recurse, un-pick.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void permute(int arr[], int n)

It must PRINT every permutation of arr on its own line, values space-separated, in lexicographic order. The values are distinct and given ascending, so a backtracking recursion that tries candidates in input order produces exactly the lex order. The harness prints nothing else.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n distinct integers in ascending order.

Output Format:
n! lines, each one permutation (space-separated), in lexicographic order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 6

questions.title: Permutation Rank in Lex Order
questions.description:
A puzzle grader receives a permutation of 1..n and must report its 1-based position (rank) in the lexicographically sorted list of ALL permutations. The rank comes from the factorial number system: at each position, every smaller unused value that could have stood there contributes (remaining positions)! skipped permutations.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long perm_rank(int arr[], int n)

arr is a permutation of the values 1..n. It must return the 1-based lexicographic rank. Walk positions left to right; before fixing arr[i], count the unused values smaller than arr[i] (call it c) and add c * (n-1-i)! to the rank, then mark arr[i] used.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: a permutation of 1..n.

Output Format:
One line with the 1-based rank.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 12

questions.title: Print Subsets With Sum S
questions.description:
A diet planner lists every meal combination from a menu whose calories sum exactly to the daily budget S. Backtracking must both COUNT the combinations and PRINT each one — pure include/exclude recursion, no loops anywhere.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void subsets_sum(int arr[], int n, int S)

It must PRINT exactly:

Line 1: K, the number of subsets of arr whose values sum to S.
Then K lines, each one qualifying subset's values space-separated, in the order produced by include-first backtracking (item i is tried as "included" before "excluded", items visited left to right). When K is 0, nothing follows the count line. The harness prints nothing else. NO loops are allowed in your code — print each subset with recursion too.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: S.

Output Format:
The count line, then K subset lines (see the exact ordering rule).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12, 1 <= value <= 100, 0 <= S <= 1200

questions.title: N-Queens Solution Count
questions.description:
A chess-training app needs the number of ways to place n non-attacking queens on an n x n board. Backtracking places one queen per row, tries each column, and undoes the placement when a branch fails — the search tree IS the recursion tree.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int nqueens(int n)

It must return the number of distinct solutions for the n-queens problem. Track occupied columns and both diagonal directions with marker arrays while recursing row by row.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of solutions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8

questions.title: Balanced Bracket Sequences
questions.description:
A config validator generates every balanced bracket sequence with n pairs, in lexicographic order ('(' sorts before ')'). Backtracking appends '(' while any remain, appends ')' only when it would not unbalance, and prints when the sequence is complete.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void brackets(int n)

It must PRINT all balanced sequences of n '(' and n ')' pairs, one per line, in lexicographic order — trying '(' before ')' at every position yields exactly that order. The harness prints nothing else. NO loops are allowed in your code.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
Catalan(n) lines, each a balanced bracket sequence, in lexicographic order.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 6
